description: Sandbox release-candidate validation coverage register (tempdoc 728, Part B/C). Projection-not-fork applied to release validation: what a clean-Sandbox round must verify DERIVES from what the app ships, instead of being remembered. scripts/sandbox/gen_coverage_brief.py reads the committed surface artifacts (route-manifest cohorts, CorePlugin.ts surface ids, coreInteractionShapes.ts) and FAILS CLOSED if any derived cohort/surface/shape is neither covered nor exempted here — so a newly-shipped surface (the /mcp and trust-panel misses that motivated this doc) can no longer be silently forgotten. Tiers: 'sandbox' = the clean-install / real-GUI / real-external-agent view only the Sandbox has; 'host' = protocol/contract correctness a host test already owns (the Sandbox still confirms reachability); 'sandbox-must-watch' = findings that cannot be CI-gated (Windows trust prompts) and are re-injected into every round's brief (Part C). Same positive-coverage shape as check-ui-step-coverage / check-declared-surfaces.

cohortCoverage.validateHow: On a clean install, confirm an EXTERNAL MCP client reaches POST /mcp. UPDATE (round 10, tempdoc 734/804): the documented Inspector CLI reachability check (`npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector --cli http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp --transport http --method tools/list`) FAILS on this build -- POST /mcp enforces the session token like every other mutating route (prod=true), the Inspector CLI has no flag for a custom auth header, the bare 401 carries no WWW-Authenticate, and the Inspector infers OAuth and demands an interactive TTY a round cannot supply. Verify reachability instead with a raw POST /mcp JSON-RPC tools/list call carrying the X-JustSearch-Session token fetched from GET /api/mcp/token (body `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list"}`) and confirm the tool set comes back; if you use the Inspector CLI anyway, record its auth-header limitation explicitly rather than reporting an unexplained failure. requiredRoutes pins POST /mcp so a token-only GET can't satisfy coverage. Protocol conformance is host-owned (McpProtocolHandlerTest); the Sandbox proves clean-install reachability + discoverability. REQUIRED PROCEDURE for the published TYPED_CONFIRM trust-gate claim (see claims[] below): the Inspector CLI's `--tool-arg` string-coerces every value and CANNOT express `justsearch_ingest`'s `paths: string[]` argument -- do not attempt tools/call through it, that procedure is unfollowable (verified against a real round; see tmp/sandbox evidence from the round that hit this). Instead run the staged driver `node <mapped folder>\mcp-client\mcp-typed-confirm.mjs --target <path>` (see `<mapped folder>\mcp-client\README.md`), which spawns the REAL shipped MCPB stdio bridge (`mcp-client\index.js`, a verbatim copy of packaging/mcpb/server/index.js) as a child process and drives `initialize` -> `notifications/initialized` -> `tools/call justsearch_ingest(paths:[<path>])` over its stdin/stdout -- the same transport a real MCP host (e.g. Claude Desktop) uses, so this exercises the actual shipped artifact. Confirm the tools/call response reports a PENDING authorization (isError:true, 'requires your approval (gate: TYPED_CONFIRM)'), not a silent/immediate ingest. The gate response text does NOT carry the pending id -- mcp-typed-confirm.mjs resolves it itself (via GET /api/advisory/authorization-pending/stream) and prints it as `PENDING_ID=<id>` right after the gate result; read that line, do not hand-scrape SSE. Resolve the pending via EITHER the GUI approval ceremony (open the live pending-authorization UI on the real shipped webview and click Approve) OR the API path -- both dispatch the ingest. REFUTED (round 11, tempdoc 734 round-11 section): an earlier version of this text claimed `execute: true` via the API was MANDATORY for an MCP-originated pending because "an MCP-originated pending has no live browser caller left to replay the capsule against" -- round 11 approved an MCP-originated pending entirely through the GUI and the ingest dispatched (docCount 405 -> 406, file searchable), so the GUI ceremony works too and the API path is not the only route. The API variant, if you use it: `POST /api/authorizations/approve` with JSON body `{"pendingId": "<id>", "execute": true}` (API-reachable, no GUI needed) -- the body key for the id is `pendingId` (AuthorizationController.handleApprove reads body.pendingId; any other key name for the id 400s), and `execute: true` makes this call dispatch the ingest immediately as part of the approval rather than only minting a consent capsule for a separate caller to replay -- useful when no GUI is available, not required when one is. A prior round's procedure named a different (wrong) body key for the id with no execute flag at all, got 400s, and misfiled the result as "approve never executes the operation" -- a false HIGH regression against this documentation defect, not the product. scripts/ci/check-sandbox-authorization-field.mjs now fails the build if that retired key name reappears here or in mcp-client-README.md. Then confirm the ingest actually proceeds after approval. `tools/list` reachability alone does NOT exercise this claim -- it is a separate, mandatory step this round must perform. STATUS (2026-07-15): a prior PowerShell driver was found to HANG waiting on the tools/call response and has been removed. Live isolation against a running dev stack independently verified: the server is fixed and conformant (notifications/initialized returns 202 Accepted with no body; unknown requests still return -32601), and the shipped bridge driven over stdio by this exact Node driver's message sequence WORKS end-to-end -- initialize succeeds, and tools/call justsearch_ingest with a real array paths returns the TYPED_CONFIRM gate response. The server, the shipped bridge, and this driver's message sequence are live-verified; the round running this procedure still must execute mcp-typed-confirm.mjs itself and report the result (including the post-approval re-check).

mustWatch.reason: A shell update must remain usable when the Engine cannot boot, reconcile owned children before replacement, and recover the existing user stores after installing the repair.
mustWatch.origin: Lane F stage B13; design section 0 decision dated 2026-09-08 permits the branch host-level proof and defers the signed installer exercise to the first post-merge installer round.
mustWatch.note: Not CI-gateable. In the first post-merge signed installer round, preserve a populated previous release data directory; induce a non-transient Engine boot failure and wait for exhausted; use the pre-API recovery update action; verify registered matching children exit before installer launch and unrelated PID identities survive; install the repair, open every inherited authoritative store (including memory and notes), preserve index count, and answer a search from the inherited index. Record source/candidate versions and stop evidence; do not treat host fixture tests as this packaged exercise.

mustWatch.reason: SmartScreen / Defender / Smart App Control / publisher-identity UI on install cannot be reproduced in CI (no clean Windows); every round records the exact prompt text/screenshots and whether automation (/S) was honored.
mustWatch.note: PARTIALLY observable since 2026-08-12: candidates are Authenticode-signed (SSL.com IV cert, CN=Elias Justus; tempdoc 760/772 sign-once chain -- opt-in CI signing + signed vendored mirrors), which retires the 'real fix is code signing; deferred by owner budget' status this entry previously carried. validateHow, signature-derived half (NOW observable): (1) installer file Properties -> Digital Signatures must show a Valid 'Elias Justus' signature (screenshot it); (2) after install, the installed-apps / uninstall entry must show publisher 'Elias Justus'; (3) any consent/trust dialog that appears must name the publisher -- an 'Unknown publisher' anywhere on a signed candidate is a FINDING, as is an elevation prompt (per-user install, ADR-0024); (4) spot-check one bundled PE (e.g. llama-server.exe or tesseract.exe) with Get-AuthenticodeSignature: expect Valid / CN=Elias Justus. Reputation half (STILL posture-blocked): genuine SmartScreen reputation verdicts cannot fire -- generate_wsb's LogonCommand force-disables Smart App Control at boot (sandbox-launch.py's generate_wsb), the folder-mounted installer never carries Mark-of-the-Web, and a young cert has no reputation history -- record that HALF as unobservable-with-reason (never as a pass) unless the round deliberately attaches MOTW via an in-sandbox download of the installer.

mustWatch.reason: An expired/already-consumed authorization pending can still render a fully convincing Authorize dialog -- typing the confirm phrase enables Approve, but clicking Approve (or Deny) silently no-ops with no grant, no error, and no way to dismiss the modal. Invisible to an API-only round (item 4 scored a clean PASS on the API); only the GUI tier surfaced it. Check remains UI-tier until/unless a host RAIL step lands.
mustWatch.origin: HIGH finding, tempdoc 727-followup smoke round, reproduced under two varied conditions (expired vs fresh pending) on the 0.2.0 build; may already be fixed on later builds but is a standing must-watch until a regression test exists

mustWatch.reason: An upgrade must not lose or corrupt the index: docCount must be unchanged pre/post upgrade, and a post-upgrade search must return hits (not silently empty).
mustWatch.origin: Charter question Q1, answered by both round 9 (docCount 255->255) and round 10 (docCount 405->405) via COMPATIBLE/FINGERPRINT_MATCH plus live oracle queries returning hits; tempdoc 734 rounds 9+10, promoted to registered coverage per tempdoc 804 Section B10 ('the generated must-touch set is byte-identical to a fresh round's' -- second round asking).
mustWatch.note: validateHow: capture docCount from GET /api/knowledge/status (or GET /api/status) immediately before running the candidate installer and again after first boot completes; the two values must match. Then run at least one oracle search and confirm hits>0, not just embeddingCompatState reading COMPATIBLE.

mustWatch.reason: Per ADR-0024 (per-user, non-elevated install; user data is retained across install/uninstall), an upgrade must preserve the user's models, index, and watched roots -- not just the install directory.
mustWatch.origin: Charter question Q2; round 9 and round 10 both confirmed models/index/watched-folders survive on disk (round 9: 12.08 GB models + 4.48 GB cuda12 runtime intact; round 10: index byte-identical, watched folders intact, skin choice survives restart), while both rounds also recorded genuine gaps (round 9: encryption not established in v0.1.0; round 10: conversations vacuous in v0.1.0) that must be recorded as gaps, not silently scored as passes. tempdoc 734 rounds 9+10; tempdoc 804 Section B10.
mustWatch.note: validateHow: before the upgrade, record the watched-roots list, model files present under the data dir, and index size/docCount. After the upgrade's first boot, diff against the same three -- all must match (survive), and any genuine gap (e.g. a feature not present in the prior release) must be stated explicitly as a gap, not folded into a blanket PASS (ADR-0024).

mustWatch.reason: The embedding-compatibility fingerprint must carry over the upgrade without forcing an unnecessary rebuild or, worse, silently treating incompatible vectors as compatible.
mustWatch.origin: Charter question Q3; both round 9 and round 10 reported embeddingCompatState reaching COMPATIBLE/FINGERPRINT_MATCH with the fingerprint byte-identical pre/post upgrade -- the healthy case. A mismatch is not itself a failure (a model change between releases legitimately changes the fingerprint) but must be an EXPLAINED mismatch, not a silent divergence. tempdoc 734 rounds 9+10; tempdoc 804 Section B10.
mustWatch.note: validateHow: read embeddingFingerprintStored/embeddingFingerprintCurrent and embeddingCompatState from GET /api/knowledge/status pre- and post-upgrade. COMPATIBLE with a byte-identical fingerprint is a clean pass; any other combination requires the round to state the explanation (e.g. a model version bump) or file it as a finding -- never leave it unexplained.

mustWatch.reason: The NSIS installer's over-install path (installing the candidate over an already-installed prior release) must detect the prior version, offer/perform a clean uninstall-then-install, and leave exactly one registry entry with no side-by-side install.
mustWatch.origin: Charter question Q4; round 9 confirmed old-version detection, uninstall-then-install, exactly one HKCU entry after, zero 0.1.0 jars left; round 10 confirmed the 'Already Installed' page detects the prior version with 'Uninstall before installing' preselected, one HKCU entry after, no elevation prompt, per-user throughout (ADR-0024). tempdoc 734 rounds 9+10; tempdoc 804 Section B10.
mustWatch.note: validateHow: before the candidate installer runs, confirm the prior release is genuinely installed (HKCU registry entry present). After the candidate installer completes, confirm exactly one registry entry exists (not two), the prior version's binaries are gone (no side-by-side install directory), and the flow stayed per-user (no elevation prompt, no HKLM entry).

mustWatch.reason: chunkEmbeddingReady (chunk-level vector queryability, GET /api/knowledge/status) must not silently regress across an upgrade -- a true-to-false flip means chunk-level RAG retrieval goes dark with no user-facing signal unless a round is specifically watching for it.
mustWatch.origin: Round 11 (tempdoc 734 round-11 section): chunkEmbeddingReady flipped True -> False across the upgrade -- the one thing that genuinely degraded that round -- and none of the four registered upgrade-survival questions (index/user-data/embedding-compat/NSIS-over-install) covers it; the registered set was 'provably incomplete'. Invented by round 11, registered per tempdoc 805 Part E / G.5.
mustWatch.note: validateHow: read chunkEmbeddingReady from GET /api/knowledge/status immediately before running the candidate installer and again after first boot completes (same before/after shape as upgrade-index-survives). true->true is a clean pass. Any other transition (true->false in particular) must be EXPLAINED -- state whether it reflects a genuine truth-telling correction (e.g. the probe method changed, tempdoc 734 round-11 section: v0.1.0 computed it from status-field counts, HEAD computes it from actual chunk_vector artifact presence) or an actual regression -- never leave a flip silently unexplained.

mustWatch.reason: The ONNX execution provider can silently fall back from GPU to CPU (Worker log: GPU session creation failed / an incomplete ORT CUDA native pack) while /api/ai/runtime/status keeps reporting a GPU variant active -- a capability-survival defect invisible to every API assertion in the coverage brief; only the Worker log knows.
mustWatch.origin: Round 11 finding F3 (ONNX GPU -> CPU fallback, the round's most actionable defect, found only because /start rule 5 says read Head AND Worker logs -- the Worker log carried 4 ERRORs the API surface reported as status: "active"). Registered per tempdoc 805 Part E / G.5.
mustWatch.note: validateHow (current, log-based): after Install AI completes and a chat/inference call runs, read the Worker log for ONNX execution-provider errors (GPU session creation failed, ORT CUDA native pack incomplete, or any CUDAExecutionProvider fallback warning) and cross-check against /api/ai/runtime/status's reported active variant -- a GPU variant reported active while the Worker log shows a CPU fallback is the defect. CONVERTS TO an API-only assertion once observed-EP fields ship on /api/ai/runtime/status (tempdoc 805 G.3, requested vs. converged EP shape) -- until then this stays log-based and sandbox-tier. UPDATE (tempdoc 805 G.3 / W3, shipped): /api/ai/runtime/status now carries OBSERVED execution-provider fields per ONNX feature -- executionProvider ('cuda'|'cpu'|'none'|'unknown'), gpuFallback, fallbackReason (the probe failure + missing DLL names) -- projected from the EncoderRuntimeExplainer derivation that backs /api/inference/encoders, and /api/ai/install/status carries repairNeeded. A future round can therefore assert this contradiction over the API: gpuFallback true (or executionProvider 'cpu' while a cuda12 variant is active) IS the defect, no Worker log reading required. Convert this entry to that API assertion once a round has confirmed the fields report correctly on a real machine. UPDATE (tempdoc 806 B.2, round-12 follow-up): the observed-EP rows now cover ALL FOUR encoders, not two -- `embed` and `splade` joined `reranker` and `citation_scorer` on /api/ai/runtime/status.onnxFeatures, sourced from the SAME EncoderRuntimeExplainer authority (the Worker policy snapshot x OrtCuda probe). Round 11 fell back to CPU on all four and round 12 could only assert two, so the Worker log stayed the sole witness for embed/splade; it no longer is. Note the honest asymmetry when asserting: the embed/splade rows carry status unknown (not inactive) until the Worker answers, because WorkerModelDiscovery.discoverAll() enumerates only reranker + citation-scorer and cannot speak for them.

mustWatch.reason: The mid-upgrade uninstall step (triggered automatically by the NSIS over-install path) presents as a standalone-titled 'Remove JustSearch from your computer' wizard with a 'Delete the application data' checkbox and an ambiguous Cancel -- indistinguishable from a real uninstall unless a round already knows it's mid-upgrade. Ticking the checkbox would destroy the user's data (16.6 GB observed in round 10) mid-upgrade.
mustWatch.origin: Round-10 finding F11 [LOW, UX] (round-9 F4 partly refuted by round-10's own re-review: the installer DOES announce uninstall-then-install via the 'Already Installed' page with a safe default preselected; what remains is this standalone wizard window). tempdoc 734 round 10; tempdoc 804 Section B10 ('F11 residue -> sandbox-must-watch (mid-upgrade uninstaller wording/data-deletion checkbox)').
mustWatch.note: validateHow: screenshot the mid-upgrade uninstall wizard the moment it appears. Confirm 'Delete the application data' is UNCHECKED by default (it was in round 10) and record the exact title/copy verbatim -- flag any wording change, since a future build could flip the default or drop the disambiguating context without anyone noticing outside a round that specifically looks for it.

mustWatch.reason: Round 19 (0.3.0 candidate 2, tempdoc 941 R19-F1): a Structured (core.extract) turn sent from the bottom mode control in a conversation that already held a Documents (rag-ask) turn, on a shell open since first paint, returned HTTP 200 and was persisted by the backend (history and thread both carried the extract user+assistant records) yet the shell cleared the prompt and kept showing the previous Document Q&A card -- no JSON frame. mustWatch.origin: Round-19 F1 [HIGH]; tempdoc 941 round 19; round-18 watch item that reproduced.
mustWatch.note: validateHow: on the shell that has been open since first paint, in the SAME conversation as an earlier Documents answer, select Structured from the bottom mode control, attach a one-property schema, send one prompt; record the authenticated POST /api/chat/dispatch count before and after.
